data.narrative:
DeepDrive is a Series B transportation-tech company that has raised $54.4M to date across seven founders. The broader transportation sector includes seven private peers of varying stages and maturity (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, The ePlane Company, and others), with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $54.4M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage transitions, yielding an implied valuation of $103M. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-set comparables: while three same-sector peers exist, none qualified under stage or valuation-tier filters (minimum three required), making broad-sector median comparison potentially misleading.

The triangulated range spans $88M (low) to $119M (high), with a median of $103M. This single-method derivation introduces material uncertainty, as it relies on stage-progression assumptions rather than market-derived multiples. Key risks to this range include company-specific metrics not visible in the supplied data (revenue, growth rate, unit economics) and the wide dispersion in transportation-sector maturity across the peer universe. The valuation should be stress-tested against actual financial performance and updated as comparable transaction data matures.
